ai.description: This slender snake reaches 1.2 meters. It is bright green with a distinct black streak through each eye and a white-bordered black postocular stripe. A faint vertebral line is often present.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Gonyosoma frenatum* is the distinct, thin black stripe running horizontally through each eye, which is absent in similar green snakes.
ai.habitat: *Gonyosoma frenatum* inhabits humid, evergreen broadleaf forests and montane regions of the Indian subcontinent, typically at elevations ranging from 500 to 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Khasi Hills Trinket Snake is primarily arboreal and diurnal, often displaying a striking defensive posture by flattening its neck to mimic a cobra when threatened.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gonyosoma frenatum* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 5–12 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing in late summer or autumn.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Gonyosoma frenatum* occurs in Northeast India, specifically in the Khasi Hills of Meghalaya and parts of Arunachal Pradesh, typically at elevations between 500–2,000m.
